open_points.subject: A13 confirmation expiry
open_points.text: “an expired one is refused and cleared by any submission that reaches the confirmation check, whatever value it gives” conflicts with “giving another value, is refused and leaves the pending value as it was”
open_points.question: When the pending confirmation has expired and the submission gives a different value, is the pending confirmation cleared or retained?
options: Clear it because every submission reaching the check clears an expired confirmation
Retain it because a different value never consumes or clears the pending confirmation

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation input binding
open_points.text: “the inputs it is bound to, and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order” does not declare that order or the canonical encoding of the values
open_points.question: What exact ordered byte representation is hashed when binding a confirmation to its inputs, including absent values, collections, text and import picks?
options: Declare one canonical ordered serialization
Hash the request representation as received
Use operation-specific encodings chosen by the implementation
open_points.default_guess: Use a specification-declared canonical serialization with operation-specific field order.

open_points.subject: A13 concurrent sign-out and requests
open_points.text: “a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs” conflicts with “The requests of one owner session that change its state ... are applied one at a time”; every valid owner request also changes `last_request`
open_points.question: May sign-out overlap an already validated request, or must it serialize behind every request that updates the session?
options: Allow overlap and let the validated request finish after sign-out
Serialize sign-out with every valid request
Serialize only confirmation, upload and submission state while allowing sign-out to overlap other requests
open_points.default_guess: Allow an already validated request to finish, while sign-out prevents only later arrivals.

open_points.subject: A13 restart during a request
open_points.text: “a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it” does not say whether a transaction committed before the process stops survives when the response was not completed
open_points.question: What counts as an interrupted request: one whose transaction has not committed, or any request whose response was not completed before restart?
options: A committed transaction survives; only uncommitted work leaves nothing
Any request without a completed response must leave nothing
open_points.default_guess: A committed transaction survives and only uncommitted work is rolled back.

open_points.subject: A04 CSRF on owner reads
open_points.text: A04 says “Every operation — read or change ... checks ... for the owner, a valid owner session, then its CSRF value”, while A13 says “Every change in the owner interface carries the CSRF protection”
open_points.question: Must an owner-interface read supply and pass the session's CSRF value, or is CSRF checked only for state-changing requests?
options: Check CSRF only on state-changing requests
Check CSRF on every owner-interface request, reads included
open_points.default_guess: Check CSRF only on state-changing requests.

open_points.subject: A04 confirmation check stage
open_points.text: A04 puts “a confirmation value where one is asked” in stage 1, while A13 also binds that value to the action, target, revision or access version and inputs whose checks otherwise occur in stages 3–5
open_points.question: Does stage 1 check only equality with the pending one-time value, or also its action, target, input and revision/access-version binding; and which failure is returned when that binding and a later check both fail?
options: Stage 1 checks the value and all binding facts
Stage 1 checks only the one-time value and binding is checked in the corresponding later stages
Each binding failure is assigned separately to the stage for its kind
open_points.default_guess: Check token equality and consume it at stage 1, then report binding failures in the stages corresponding to target, values and version.

open_points.subject: A01 request-id form
open_points.text: “printable text of at most 128 characters” does not define which Unicode or ASCII characters count as printable or whether equivalent Unicode spellings compare as the same request id
open_points.question: What exact character repertoire and equality rule must a request id satisfy?
options: Printable ASCII with byte-for-byte equality
Unicode characters classified as printable with code-point equality
Any non-control Unicode text with normalized equality
open_points.default_guess: Accept printable ASCII only and compare it exactly.

open_points.subject: A14 entry existence invariant
open_points.text: “entry e exists <=> accepted action a ... and e written in the transaction of a” is stated without a time qualification, although A15 later erases entries and R0-89 may restore a history that lacks later entries
open_points.question: Is the equivalence meant only immediately after the action commits, or must it characterize the entries currently present after erasure and restore?
options: It applies at the action's commit; later erasure or loss may remove the entry
It characterizes current entries and must include conditions excluding erased or lost entries
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an invariant at commit time and separately specify later removal or loss.

open_points.subject: A16 file digest
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and `closure.file_digest = digest(f)` do not declare the digest algorithm or whether it is computed over the uploaded bytes or a parsed canonical form
open_points.question: How exactly is the import file digest calculated and compared?
options: A declared cryptographic digest over the exact uploaded bytes
A digest over a canonical parsed representation
A release-selected algorithm and representation
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: A16 post-import backup timing
open_points.text: A16 says “right after it Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule”, while A18 says “an owner-only start makes no run” and that a repeated import's backup “is made at the next start with the tokens”
open_points.question: If an import is accepted during an owner-only recovery start, is its backup attempted immediately or deferred until the next start with service tokens?
options: Attempt it immediately despite owner-only mode
Defer it until the next start with service tokens
Do not permit import during owner-only mode
open_points.default_guess: Defer it until the next start with service tokens.

open_points.subject: A17 owner-only configuration test
open_points.text: Rule 1 permits “for an owner-only start, none of the four” service tokens, but required test 1 says “A configuration without Client Portal's token stops the start” without excluding the permitted no-token configuration
open_points.question: Does the missing-Client-Portal test apply only when at least one service token is configured, or must a no-token configuration also fail?
options: No tokens is the permitted owner-only mode; any partial token set fails
Every missing service token fails, so owner-only mode is not actually permitted
open_points.default_guess: Permit exactly zero tokens for owner-only mode and reject every partial set.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” does not specify an authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation, key derivation, file format or what metadata is authenticated
open_points.question: What exact cryptographic construction and authenticated backup format must implementations use?
options: Declare one authenticated-encryption scheme and format
Allow any authenticated-encryption scheme meeting stated properties
Permit encryption without a specified integrity mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption format with random nonces and authenticated metadata.

open_points.subject: A18 backup publication and status recovery
open_points.text: A backup “become[s] a kept backup only when complete” and each run separately “writes its outcome and instant to a status file”, but no atomic order or restart reconciliation is stated
open_points.question: After a crash between publishing a checked backup and updating the status file, which outcome must the owner interface show and does that day count as having a backup?
options: The kept backup is authoritative and status is reconstructed from it
The status file is authoritative and the backup is discarded or ignored
Backup publication and status update must be one atomic operation
open_points.default_guess: Treat the kept checked backup as authoritative and reconstruct stale status on restart.

open_points.subject: A18 recovery ordering
open_points.text: Rule 10 first says the owner “brings each Customer and project to the state ... and erases audit entries” and then says “an import the owner repeats then ... comes first”
open_points.question: During recovery from a backup predating the import, must the repeated import occur before or after replaying retention actions and the audit cutoff?
options: Repeat the import first, then reconcile imported and existing records and erase audit entries
Reconcile the restored records first, then repeat the import
Apply reconciliation both before and after the import
open_points.default_guess: Repeat the import first, then reconcile all resulting records and finally apply the audit cutoff.

open_points.subject: A18 recovered audit cutoff
open_points.text: “erases audit entries before the latest date the owner erased by” does not say whether “latest” means the most recently recorded erasure action or the greatest cutoff date ever used
open_points.question: Which cutoff is replayed when later audit-erasure actions used non-monotonic dates?
options: The greatest cutoff date ever accepted
The cutoff from the chronologically latest erasure action
Replay every recorded erasure action in order
open_points.default_guess: Use the greatest cutoff date ever accepted.

open_points.subject: OwnerSession uploaded file after another session imports
open_points.text: M11 says an uploaded import file is “dropped when the import is accepted”, while A16 says after another session accepts the import “a file another session keeps stays until that session ends”
open_points.question: Does acceptance of any import drop uploaded files from all owner sessions, or only from the session that confirmed it?
options: Drop only the confirming session's file
Drop every session's uploaded import file when the closure is created
open_points.default_guess: Drop only the confirming session's file; other sessions retain theirs until replacement or session end.

open_points.subject: R0-89 retention-review record for audit erasure
open_points.text: R0-89 says the governance record names “each action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched”, but also requires it to carry “the latest date audit entries were erased by”; an audit-log erasure touches neither a customer nor a project
open_points.question: How is an audit-entry erasure represented in the retention-review record when it has no `customer_ref` or `project_id`?
options: Allow audit erasure records with no subject and a cutoff date
Give the audit log a separate subject identifier
Exclude audit erasures from the per-action records and store only a separate cutoff
open_points.default_guess: Allow a subjectless audit-erasure record carrying its cutoff date.

open_points.subject: R0-89 missing recovery evidence
open_points.text: R0-89 says “Where the retention record or the kept export is missing, what the restored store holds stands until the owner corrects it”, while A18 requires reconciliation and any repeated import before service tokens are configured
open_points.question: May the restored instance leave owner-only mode and serve services when the retention record or required export is missing, or must it remain owner-only until the missing evidence is corrected?
options: Remain owner-only until the evidence is restored and reconciliation completes
Permit service startup with the restored state standing as it is
Permit service startup only when the missing evidence affects no record currently in the store
open_points.default_guess: Keep the instance owner-only until the missing evidence is corrected.
